It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where “earthly kingdoms go the way of all flesh” through the “noise and tumult” of war, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the distinction between the world’s fragile truce and the Savior’s eternal repose in this hour? [1-5]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who promise a “spiritual placebo” of peace while the “horrible pit” of conflict widens, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “history is His story”—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory that no machine or monarch can truly narrate? [2, 6-10]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with a culture that “mocks, vilifies, and censures” the Gospel, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by reminding us that “your life is not your own” [1, 11-15].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the absence of earthly peace is not an “administrative anomaly” but a context in which we must “examine everything carefully” to distinguish the “glittery lookalike from the genuine commodity” [1, 8, 16-18].

***

### **Section 1: The False Peace of the World’s Deception**

**Verse**
“ ‘They have also healed the hurt of My people slightly, saying, “Peace, peace!” When there is no peace’ ” (Jeremiah 6:14). [19].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that the “record of history” reveals a recurring “human tendency” to seek “relief for their anxieties through a false peace” which is often a “spiritual justification for self-indulgence” [6, 20, 21]. The Reformed faith—upheld by **John MacArthur**—notes that “the peace of the wicked is born of delusion,” for “there is no peace for the wicked,” and their “seeming peace... is not from the knowledge of [their] happiness, but the ignorance of [their] danger” (Isaiah 48:22; Proverbs 14:12) [20, 22-24]. When the prophets’ critics promised safety, they were offering “cleverly devised myths” that acted as a “cradle of security” on the “precipice of hell” (2 Peter 1:16) [25-27]. This false peace is a “spirit of fraud” that “muffles the truth of God’s Word” with “trivial diversions” [1, 28].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “market-driven strategy” that promises “temporal happiness” through a “balanced checkbook” or a “pulpit-throne,” for “the world is passing away along with its desires” (1 John 2:17) [2, 11, 29, 30]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word,” for “the Word of our God stands forever” while human “psychology and philosophy” vanish like smoke (Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2; Isaiah 40:8) [1, 31-34].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious leaders” often relied on “national greatness” and “military skill” as “temporal signs” of favor, yet Jesus warned that they “pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith” (Matthew 23:23) [35-38]. The New Testament **revises** our standing, showing that we are “sojourners and pilgrims” whose “citizenship is in heaven,” looking for a “city whose builder and maker is God” (1 Peter 2:11; Philippians 3:20; Hebrews 11:10) [2, 31, 38-43].

***

### **Section 2: The Divine Origin of Christ’s Peace**

**Verse**
“ ‘Peace I leave with you, My peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Do not let your heart be troubled, nor let it be fearful’ ” (John 14:27). [44-46].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Charles Spurgeon**—asserts that “godly peace has nothing to do with human beings or human circumstances,” because it is an “attribute of God” Himself [47-49]. Christ’s peace is the “repose of the soul who trusts in [His] finished work,” a “lavish endowment” that “surpasses all comprehension” (John 19:30; Philippians 4:7) [50-53]. While the world’s peace is “very fragile” and “can be destroyed instantly by failure, doubt, or fear,” God’s peace is “unbreakable, unassailable, [and] transcendent,” rooted in the truth that “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan” (Job 42:2) [1, 13, 45, 54, 55]. This peace is a “sovereign, gracious gift” for those who “walk by the Spirit” and “discipline [their] mind[s]” to dwell on “whatever things are true” (Galatians 5:16; Philippians 4:8) [14, 31, 44, 56, 57].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for the “Lord of peace Himself [will] give you peace always in every way” (2 Thessalonians 3:16) [1, 13, 31, 58, 59]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” recognizing that “God causes all things to work together for good to those who love God,” even when you feel “hard-pressed on every side” (1 Corinthians 9:27; Romans 8:28; 2 Corinthians 4:8) [1, 2, 60-64].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, the “Sabbath” was a “sacred ordained day” to celebrate the Creator, yet it was often turned into a “minefield” of “unwritten... taboos” [65-67]. The New Testament **revises** this, revealing that “everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ,” granting believers a “portable temple” of peace where “your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit” (1 Corinthians 6:19; Hebrews 4:10) [1-3, 11, 38, 67-72].

***

### **Section 3: Speaking Peace in the Aftermath of War**

**Verse**
“He shall judge between the nations, And rebuke many people; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore” (Isaiah 2:4). [73, 74].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—upheld by **Voddie Baucham**—teaches that in the aftermath of war, the church must not offer “merely moral” solutions but point to the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [2, 7, 31, 75-78]. We are to speak of a “better world than this one,” where “perfect justice will come” and “God will wipe away every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4) [36, 58, 75, 78-81]. The church’s “sole objective” is to lead people to a “saving knowledge of Jesus Christ,” for while governments wield the sword to “punish evildoers,” only the Gospel “reconciles... all things to Himself” (Romans 13:4; Colossians 1:20) [1, 82-85].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the Form of this world is passing away” and the “Lord Savior” will ultimately “judge the earth” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 1 Corinthians 7:31; Psalm 98:9) [1, 8, 13, 55, 58, 68, 75, 78, 86-88]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by “resting upon the surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” His “everlasting dominion” over the nations is “secure” (Psalm 138:2; Daniel 7:14) [1, 8, 34, 55, 58, 68, 89-99].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Stewardship**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, Israel was a “man of war” under the “Mosaic economy,” yet they were commanded to “seek the peace of the city where I have caused you to be carried away captive” (Jeremiah 29:7; 1 Chronicles 28:3) [38, 100-102]. The New Testament **revises** the “warfare” of the saints, teaching that “the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh,” for we are a “church militant” that conquers “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony” rather than through “carnal weaponry” (2 Corinthians 10:4; Revelation 12:11) [1, 2, 31, 38, 86, 90, 103-105].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). America has but one destiny: to go the way of all the other nations. No human kingdom will endure forever because built into it are the sinful seeds of its own destruction: “Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people” (Prov. 14:34); “In the generations gone by He permitted all the nations to go their own ways” (Acts 14:16).
